name: Linux kernel

eras.quote: The Linux Kernel is provided under: SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0 WITH Linux-syscall-note

editorial_view: Programs that only call the kernel through normal system calls are not affected by its GPL. Kernel modules and modified kernels you distribute must come with source under GPL-2.0.
notes:
github.com/torvalds/linux is the mainline mirror of git.kernel.org. COPYING points to LICENSES/ and Documentation/process/license-rules.rst: individual files may carry other GPL-2.0-compatible licenses (for example dual BSD/GPL drivers and UAPI headers). The SPDX ID GPL-2.0 in COPYING is the deprecated form of GPL-2.0-only.
Steward detail: The Linux kernel community; Linus Torvalds maintains mainline. Copyright stays with individual contributors.

name: Android Open Source Project (AOSP)

eras.quote: NOTICE file corresponding to the section 4 d of the Apache License, Version 2.0, in this case for the Android-specific code.

editorial_view: Most of the Android platform is Apache-2.0, so device makers can ship modified userland code without publishing it; the Linux kernel inside is GPL-2.0 and its changes must be published when distributed. Google Mobile Services and Play apps are not part of AOSP and are licensed separately.
notes:
AOSP has no single top-level LICENSE: it is hundreds of repositories, each with its own license. The NOTICE file fetched at android-17.0.0_r1 in platform/frameworks/base (which also carries MODULE_LICENSE_APACHE2) confirms the Apache-2.0 part only; the kernel part rests on the separate kernel repositories and AOSP's licensing page (https://source.android.com/docs/setup/about/licenses), so the combined expression is marked Not re-verified. Many AOSP components use other licenses (BSD in bionic, for example).
Steward detail: Google LLC, through the Android Open Source Project.

name: FreeBSD

eras.quote: The compilation of software known as FreeBSD is distributed under the following terms:

editorial_view: Permissive: you can build closed products on FreeBSD as long as you keep the copyright notices.
notes:
COPYRIGHT covers the FreeBSD compilation under BSD-2-Clause and reproduces the 4.4BSD-Lite (University of California) terms; individual components (contrib/, some drivers, the toolchain) carry their own licenses, including some GPL code in contrib. Older releases used a BSD-4-Clause-style compilation notice; not modelled.
Steward detail: The FreeBSD Project (supported by the FreeBSD Foundation).

name: OpenBSD

eras.quote: Below is an example license to be used for new code in OpenBSD, modeled after the ISC license.

editorial_view: Permissive throughout; new OpenBSD code uses an ISC-style license and the inherited BSD code is BSD-licensed, so closed products can build on it with notices kept.
notes: OpenBSD has no top-level LICENSE file and the GitHub mirror has no release tags, so the source is share/misc/license.template at a pinned mirror commit; it confirms only that new code uses an ISC-style license. The base system mixes ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause (4.4BSD) and some other licenses (see https://www.openbsd.org/policy.html). The expression is a summary, not a file statement, so it is Not re-verified. The current data's 'ISC AND BSD-2-Clause' omits the BSD-3-Clause Berkeley code.

name: XNU (Darwin kernel)

eras.quote: APPLE PUBLIC SOURCE LICENSE Version 2.0 - August 6, 2003

editorial_view: APSL-2.0 is a file-level copyleft with a network-use clause: modified XNU files you deploy or distribute must be published. macOS itself is proprietary and is not covered.
notes: Some XNU files (BSD-derived code, Mach) carry their own notices. Releases before 2003 used APSL 1.x; not modelled.

name: Microsoft Windows
editorial_view: Proprietary: use is governed by the Microsoft license terms for your edition and channel (retail, OEM or volume licensing), including limits on virtualization and transfer.
notes: No public source or LICENSE file exists. The source is Microsoft's license-terms portal, which was not fetched (it blocks automated requests); terms differ by edition, version and purchase channel.

name: GNU C Library (glibc)

eras.quote: GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 2.1, February 1999

editorial_view: Linking your program dynamically against glibc, as almost every Linux program does, places no license obligations on your code. Shipping a modified glibc means publishing those changes under the LGPL.
notes:
At glibc-2.44 COPYING.LIB is a symlink to COPYING.LESSERv2 (LGPL-2.1 text); README says 'See the file COPYING.LIB for copying conditions'. The 'or later' comes from the per-file headers, not from COPYING.LESSERv2. LICENSES lists the few files under other notices. Fetched by a shallow git clone of the tag (the gitweb URL is behind bot protection). Very old releases (before about 2.2) used the GNU Library GPL 2.0; not modelled.
Steward detail: The GNU Project; glibc maintainers (much of the copyright is held by the Free Software Foundation).

name: musl libc

eras.quote: musl as a whole is licensed under the following standard MIT license:

editorial_view: Permissive, including for static linking: keep the copyright notice and you can ship musl inside closed binaries.
notes:
COPYRIGHT lists a few files under other permissive terms (public domain and BSD-style). Early pre-1.0 releases used LGPL; not modelled.
Steward detail: Rich Felker and the musl contributors.

name: GCC runtime libraries (libgcc, libstdc++)

eras.quote: GCC RUNTIME LIBRARY EXCEPTION Version 3.1, 31 March 2009

editorial_view: Programs compiled with GCC can be distributed under any license even though they link libgcc and libstdc++, as long as an eligible compilation process was used. The compiler itself is GPL-3.0-or-later.
notes:
Source is the official GitHub mirror of gcc.gnu.org/git (the gitweb raw URL is behind bot protection); COPYING3 holds the GPL-3.0 text. The runtime exception arrived with GCC 4.4 (2009); earlier releases used GPL-2.0 with the older libgcc exception, not modelled.
Steward detail: The GNU Project / Free Software Foundation.

name: LLVM / Clang

eras.quote: LLVM Release License ============================================================================== University of Illinois/NCSA Open Source License
The LLVM Project is under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions:

editorial_view: Permissive with a patent grant; the LLVM exception means binaries compiled with Clang carry no attribution duty for runtime code. Keep notices when you redistribute LLVM itself.
notes:
From LLVM 9 the LICENSE.TXT still reproduces the 'Legacy LLVM License' (NCSA) for code not yet relicensed; checked again at llvmorg-23.1.6 (unchanged headline). The relicensing commit landed 2019-01-19 on the main branch; LLVM 8.x releases (including 8.0.1, July 2019) shipped under NCSA.
Steward detail: The LLVM Foundation and LLVM contributors.

name: OpenJDK

eras.quote: "CLASSPATH" EXCEPTION TO THE GPL

editorial_view: Running any Java program on OpenJDK, and shipping OpenJDK with an application, does not put your application under the GPL thanks to the Classpath exception. Oracle's own JDK builds are under separate Oracle terms.
notes:
LICENSE is the GPL-2.0 text followed by the Classpath exception, which applies only to files whose header says Oracle designates them as subject to it; a few tools and files are plain GPL-2.0. Vendor builds (Temurin, Corretto, Oracle JDK) add their own terms.
Steward detail: Oracle leads OpenJDK, with community contributors.

name: CPython

eras.quote: Python software and documentation are licensed under the Python Software Foundation License Version 2.

editorial_view: Permissive: you can embed or ship Python in closed products; keep the license notice and summarise changes if you modify it.
notes: LICENSE also carries the historical BeOpen, CNRI and CWI licenses for older code (SPDX models the full stack as Python-2.0), and states that since 3.8.6 documentation code is dual licensed PSF-2.0 or 0BSD. Bundled libraries (OpenSSL, expat, libffi and others) keep their own licenses. Releases before 2.1 predate the PSF license; not modelled.

name: Node.js

eras.quote: Node.js is licensed for use as follows:

editorial_view: Permissive. Your real exposure is in the npm packages you install, which have their own licenses and should be scanned.
notes: LICENSE is MIT for Node.js followed by the licenses of bundled dependencies (V8, OpenSSL, ICU, libuv, npm and others).

name: React

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004
BSD License For React software
MIT License

editorial_view: Current React is MIT, so it is low risk. If you still ship React 15.6.1 or older, it came with a BSD license plus a patent grant that ends if you sue Facebook over patents.
notes:
The BSD era shipped a separate PATENTS file ('Additional Grant of Patent Rights', revised to Version 2 in commit b8ba8c83, 2015-04-10, checked at v0.12.0 and v15.6.1); it has no SPDX ID, so it is written here as LicenseRef-Facebook-Patents. 15.6.2 was released under MIT alongside 16.0.0. Checked again at v19.3.1: MIT. Governance changes after 2025 are not reflected in the steward line, which follows the LICENSE copyright notice.
Steward detail: Meta Platforms, Inc. (copyright holder named in LICENSE).

name: Vue.js

eras.quote: The MIT License (MIT)

editorial_view: Permissive: keep the notice and use it anywhere.
notes:
vuejs/core is Vue 3; Vue 2 lived in vuejs/vue, also MIT.
Steward detail: Evan You and the Vue contributors.

name: Angular

eras.quote: The MIT License

editorial_view: Permissive: keep the notice and use it anywhere.
notes: Covers Angular 2 and later. AngularJS (1.x) is a separate repository (angular/angular.js), also MIT.

name: Qt (open-source offer)

eras.quote: You may use, distribute and copy the Qt Toolkit under the terms of GNU Lesser General Public License version 2.1, which is displayed below.
GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 29 June 2007

editorial_view: Using Qt's open-source offer in a closed product means meeting LGPL-3.0 (dynamic linking or relinkable objects, and letting users replace Qt, which matters on locked devices) or buying a commercial license. Some Qt add-on modules and tools are GPL-3.0 only.
notes:
Qt has no single LICENSE file; the expression comes from the per-file headers of qtbase, checked at v5.4.0, v5.6.3 ('LGPL 2.1 or version 3' plus the Qt LGPL Exception 1.1 in LGPL_EXCEPTION.txt), v5.7.0 (LGPL-3.0, or GPL-2.0 or GPL-3.0) and v6.12.1 (SPDX: LicenseRef-Qt-Commercial OR LGPL-3.0-only OR GPL-2.0-only OR GPL-3.0-only). Qt 5.0 to 5.3 (LGPL-2.1 with exception or GPL-3.0) and Qt 4 and earlier are not modelled. Tools and tests in qtbase are GPL-3.0-only WITH Qt-GPL-exception-1.0 per REUSE.toml. The Qt-LGPL-exception-1.1 ID needs a license record. The current data's 'LGPL-3.0-only OR GPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Proprietary' omits GPL-2.0-only and folds in the commercial offer, now split into qt-commercial.
Steward detail: The Qt Company; the KDE Free Qt Foundation agreement requires Qt to stay available under open-source terms.

name: Qt (commercial license)

eras.quote: Licensees holding valid commercial Qt licenses may use this software in accordance with the the terms contained in a written agreement between you and The Qt Company.

editorial_view: A paid license from The Qt Company that removes the LGPL and GPL obligations; terms (per developer, per device, distribution fees) are set by your agreement.
notes: The LicenseRef-Qt-Commercial.txt file at the tag only points to the written agreement and https://www.qt.io/terms-conditions; the agreement itself was not reviewed. The quote reproduces the file's own typo ('the the').

name: FFmpeg (default build)

eras.quote: Most files in FFmpeg are under the GNU Lesser General Public License version 2.1 or later (LGPL v2.1+).

editorial_view: A default build is LGPL-2.1-or-later: link it dynamically (or allow relinking) and your application can stay closed. Check the configure flags of every build you ship, since they decide the license.
notes:
Codec patents are a separate question from the copyright license. Optional external libraries pulled in at configure time keep their own licenses.
Steward detail: The FFmpeg developers (copyright held by contributors).

name: FFmpeg (--enable-gpl build)

eras.quote: None of these parts are used by default, you have to explicitly pass `--enable-gpl` to configure to activate them. In this case, FFmpeg's license changes to GPL v2+.

editorial_view: A build configured with --enable-gpl is GPL-2.0-or-later as a whole: distributing it, or an application linked to it, requires GPL terms and source. Builds with --enable-nonfree cannot be redistributed.
notes:
Adding --enable-version3 moves the build to (L)GPL-3.0-or-later, which some external libraries require; --enable-nonfree produces a binary that LICENSE.md says is unredistributable.
Steward detail: The FFmpeg developers (copyright held by contributors).

name: OpenSSL

eras.quote: The OpenSSL toolkit stays under a double license, i.e. both the conditions of the OpenSSL License and the original SSLeay license apply to the toolkit.
Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004

editorial_view: OpenSSL 3.0 and later are Apache-2.0: permissive, with a patent grant, and compatible with GPL-3.0 but not GPL-2.0-only. OpenSSL 1.x carries the old OpenSSL/SSLeay terms, with an advertising clause and GPL incompatibility.
notes: There was no 2.x release. The relicensing was announced in March 2017 and applied on 2018-12-06 to the branch that became 3.0.0; 1.1.1 and earlier stay on the old license. SPDX 'OpenSSL' covers the combined OpenSSL and SSLeay licenses and needs a license record. Checked again at openssl-4.1.0: Apache-2.0.

name: PostgreSQL

eras.quote: PostgreSQL Database Management System (also known as Postgres, formerly known as Postgres95)

editorial_view: Permissive, similar to MIT/BSD: you can embed, modify or offer it as a service with no source obligations.
notes: github.com/postgres/postgres is the official mirror of git.postgresql.org. Extensions and tools in the ecosystem have their own licenses.

name: MySQL (Community)

eras.quote: This software is released under version 2 of the GNU General Public License (GPLv2), as set forth below, with the following additional permissions:

editorial_view: Running MySQL as your application's database does not affect your code. Distributing MySQL itself, or a program linked to its client library, brings GPL-2.0 obligations unless you buy Oracle's commercial license.
notes: LICENSE adds a permission to link with separately licensed software such as OpenSSL, and states that the bundled client library (libmysqlclient, Connector/C) is also subject to the Universal FOSS Exception 1.0. Oracle also sells MySQL under commercial terms (and an Enterprise Edition with closed components); that offer is not a file in the repository and is not modelled, so the current data's 'OR LicenseRef-Proprietary' is dropped from the expression. Oracle 'elects' GPLv2 only where third-party code offers a choice of GPL versions. MariaDB is a separate project.

name: SQLite

eras.quote: SQLite Is Public Domain

editorial_view: No license obligations. Organisations that need a formal license for legal reasons can buy a warranty of title from the SQLite developers.
notes:
github.com/sqlite/sqlite is the official Git mirror of the Fossil repository. LICENSE.md notes that a few non-core files in the repository are under other open-source licenses.
Steward detail: D. Richard Hipp and the SQLite developers (Hwaci).

name: MongoDB (Community Server)

eras.quote: it under the terms of the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3, as published by the Free Software Foundation.
Server Side Public License VERSION 1, OCTOBER 16, 2018

editorial_view: Using MongoDB as the database behind your own application is fine. Offering MongoDB itself as a service triggers SSPL section 13, which requires releasing the source of the whole service stack, so in practice that needs a commercial license.
notes: The README at r4.0.4 says all versions released after 2018-10-16, including patch fixes for older lines, are under SSPL; so 3.6.9, 3.4.18 and later patches are SSPL even though their version numbers fall before 4.0.4, as are dev releases from 4.1.5. The AGPL-era license file adds an OpenSSL linking exception and a clarification about management software. Drivers are Apache-2.0 and separate. Checked again at r9.0.8: SSPL-1.0. Debian and Fedora do not accept SSPL as a free license.

name: Redis

eras.quote: Redistribution and use in source and binary forms, with or without modification, are permitted provided that the following conditions are met:
Starting on March 20th, 2024, Redis follows a dual-licensing model with all Redis project code contributions under version 7.4 and subsequent releases
Starting with Redis 8, Redis Open Source is moving to a tri-licensing model

editorial_view: Redis 7.2 and earlier stay BSD-3-Clause. From 7.4 you choose RSALv2 or SSPL-1.0, neither of them open source; from 8.0 AGPL-3.0 is a third option, so an open-source project can use Redis 8 under AGPL.
notes: Checked: 7.2.4 and 7.2.17 COPYING (BSD-3-Clause), 7.4.0, 8.0.0 and 8.12.0 LICENSE.txt. The 7.2 line kept receiving BSD-licensed patch releases after 7.4 shipped.

name: Valkey

eras.quote: BSD 3-Clause License

editorial_view: Permissive BSD-3-Clause, like Redis 7.2 and earlier: keep the notices and use it anywhere, including as a managed service.
notes:
Forked from Redis 7.2.4 (the valkey repository carries tags from 7.2.4 onward). Checked at 7.2.4 and 9.2.0.
Steward detail: The Valkey project under the Linux Foundation.

name: Elasticsearch

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004
Source code in this repository is variously licensed under the Apache License Version 2.0, an Apache compatible license, or the Elastic License.
The default throughout the repository is a dual license under the Server Side Public License, v 1 and the Elastic License 2.0

eras.license_expression: (AGPL-3.0-only OR SSPL-1.0 OR Elastic-2.0) AND Elastic-2.0
eras.quote: a triple license under the "GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only", "the Server Side Public License, v 1", and the "Elastic License 2.0"

editorial_view: Up to 7.10.2 the Apache-2.0 '-oss' builds are fully open source. From 8.16, code outside x-pack can be taken under AGPL-3.0, but x-pack code (in the default distribution) is Elastic License 2.0 only, which bars offering Elasticsearch as a managed service.
notes:
Each LICENSE.txt says the default license applies unless a file header says otherwise and that some code is solely under the Elastic License, found only in the x-pack folder; the 'AND Elastic-2.0' (or AND Elastic License 1.0 for 6.3 to 7.10) term reflects that. From 6.3 to 7.10 the '-oss' artifacts excluded x-pack and were Apache-2.0 only. The 2021 change was announced 2021-01-14 and took effect in 7.11.0 (Elastic License 2.0 replaced 1.0 in commit a92a647b before release; see https://www.elastic.co/blog/elastic-license-v2). Checked: v6.2.4, v6.3.0, v7.10.2, v7.11.0, v8.15.5, v8.16.0, v9.5.7. The current data's 'Elastic-2.0 OR SSPL-1.0 OR AGPL-3.0-only' omits the x-pack ELv2-only term. Elastic License 1.0 needs a license record.
Steward detail: Elastic N.V. (Elasticsearch B.V.).

name: Kibana

eras.quote: Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
Source code in this repository is variously licensed under the Apache License Version 2.0, an Apache compatible license, or the Elastic License.
The default throughout the repository is a dual license under the Server Side Public License, v 1 and the Elastic License 2.0

eras.license_expression: (AGPL-3.0-only OR SSPL-1.0 OR Elastic-2.0) AND Elastic-2.0
eras.quote: a triple license under the "GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only", "the Server Side Public License, v 1", and the "Elastic License 2.0"

editorial_view: Same pattern as Elasticsearch: from 8.16 code outside x-pack can be used under AGPL-3.0, but the default distribution includes x-pack code that is Elastic License 2.0 only, which bars offering Kibana as a managed service.
notes:
Before 6.3 the file was LICENSE.md. The 2021 change came in two commits: 170a2956 (2021-01-20, SSPL and Elastic License) and 4584a8b5 (2021-02-04, Elastic License 2.0), both before 7.11.0. Checked: v6.2.4, v6.3.0, v7.10.2, v7.11.0, v8.15.5, v8.16.0, v9.5.7. Category is observability because Kibana is the Elastic Stack UI; the relicensing log groups it with Elasticsearch.
Steward detail: Elastic N.V. (Elasticsearch B.V.).

name: OpenSearch

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004

editorial_view: Permissive Apache-2.0: keep NOTICE files and mark changes; offering it as a managed service is allowed.
notes:
Fork of Elasticsearch 7.10.2, announced 2021-01-21 and launched 2021-04-12 (relicensing log). Version numbering restarted at 1.0.0.
Steward detail: OpenSearch Software Foundation (Linux Foundation).

name: OpenSearch Dashboards

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004

editorial_view: Permissive Apache-2.0: keep NOTICE files and mark changes; offering it as a managed service is allowed.
notes:
Fork of Kibana 7.10.2, launched with OpenSearch on 2021-04-12. Added because the relicensing log names the OpenSearch fork of Elasticsearch/Kibana.
Steward detail: OpenSearch Software Foundation (Linux Foundation).

name: Terraform

eras.quote: Mozilla Public License, version 2.0
Licensed Work: Terraform 1.6.0. The Licensed Work is (c) 2023 HashiCorp, Inc.

editorial_view: Terraform 1.5.x and earlier are MPL-2.0. From 1.6, BUSL-1.1 allows production use unless you offer Terraform to third parties as a hosted or embedded product that competes with the licensor's paid versions; each version converts to MPL-2.0 four years after publication.
notes:
Checked: v1.5.5, v1.5.7 (MPL-2.0), v1.6.0, v1.17.2 (BUSL-1.1). Commit 4eba7c05 (2026-03-11) changed the Licensor to International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) and rewrote the Additional Use Grant to define 'competitive offering' (paid products that significantly overlap; unpaid products are not competitive). 1.6.0 was published 2023-10-04, so its MPL-2.0 conversion falls in October 2027. Providers and most HashiCorp SDKs and libraries stayed MPL-2.0.
Steward detail: IBM (BUSL licensor named in LICENSE since March 2026; formerly HashiCorp, Inc.).

name: Vault

eras.quote: Mozilla Public License, version 2.0
Licensed Work: Vault Version 1.14.9 or later.

editorial_view: Vault 1.14.8 and earlier are MPL-2.0. Later versions are BUSL-1.1: production use is allowed unless you offer Vault to third parties as a hosted or embedded product that competes with the licensor's paid versions.
notes:
The first BUSL minor release was 1.15.0 (main branch changed 2023-08-11). The 1.14 patch line stayed MPL-2.0 through 1.14.8; 1.14.9 and later 1.14 patches carry BUSL (commit 48ab1eae, 2024-01-02, 'EOY license fixes 1.14.x'; LICENSE reads 'Vault Version 1.14.9 or later'). Checked: v1.14.0 to v1.14.5, v1.14.8 (MPL), v1.14.9, v1.14.10, v1.15.0, v2.2.2 (BUSL). Current LICENSE names IBM as licensor (commit 610f0e6a, 2026-03-26).
Steward detail: IBM (BUSL licensor named in LICENSE; formerly HashiCorp, Inc.).

name: Consul

eras.quote: Mozilla Public License, version 2.0
Licensed Work: Consul Version 1.16.5 or later.

editorial_view: Consul 1.16.4 and earlier are MPL-2.0. Later versions are BUSL-1.1: production use is allowed unless you offer Consul to third parties as a hosted or embedded product that competes with the licensor's paid versions.
notes:
The first BUSL minor release was 1.17.0; the 1.16 patch line stayed MPL-2.0 through 1.16.4, and 1.16.5 and later carry BUSL (commit 057c8db7, 2024-01-02). Checked: v1.16.0 to v1.16.4 (MPL), v1.16.5, v1.16.7, v1.17.0, v2.1.0 (BUSL). Current LICENSE names IBM as licensor (commit 8197dfca, 2026-03-18). No fork is named in the relicensing log.
Steward detail: IBM (BUSL licensor named in LICENSE; formerly HashiCorp, Inc.).

name: OpenTofu

eras.quote: Mozilla Public License, version 2.0

editorial_view: MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: you can use and embed OpenTofu, including as a hosted service, and must share changes only to its own MPL files when you distribute them.
notes:
Forked from the Terraform main branch at 8a085b42, the last commit before the BUSL change (Terraform then in 1.6.0 pre-release), so it is often described as a fork of Terraform 1.5.x. Announced as OpenTF in August 2023; Linux Foundation launch 2023-09-20 (https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/announcing-opentofu). First stable release 1.6.0.
Steward detail: The OpenTofu project under the Linux Foundation.

name: OpenBao

eras.quote: Mozilla Public License, version 2.0

editorial_view: MPL-2.0 file-level copyleft: you can use, embed and host OpenBao, sharing changes to its own MPL files when you distribute them.
notes:
Forked from Vault's main branch at bfe89a40, the last commit before the BUSL change (Vault then at 1.15.0-beta1). 'since' is the repository creation and first working-group meeting date (2023-11-09); public announcement followed in December 2023 under LF Edge, and the project later moved to OpenSSF. First stable release v2.0.0 (2024-07-17).
Steward detail: The OpenBao project under OpenSSF (Linux Foundation).

name: Kubernetes

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004

editorial_view: Permissive Apache-2.0 with a patent grant: keep notices and mark changes.
notes:
Vendored dependencies keep their own licenses; distributions and managed services add their own terms.
Steward detail: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (Linux Foundation).

name: Grafana

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004
GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 19 November 2007

editorial_view: Running unmodified Grafana, even for customers, has no source obligation. If you modify Grafana and let users interact with it over a network, AGPL-3.0 requires offering them your modified source.
notes: The relicensing commit landed 2021-04-20 on main; 7.5.x patch releases (checked 7.5.0, 7.5.17) stayed Apache-2.0 and 8.0.0 was the first AGPL release. README at v13.3.1 says 'Grafana is distributed under AGPL-3.0-only' with Apache-2.0 exceptions (plugins SDKs, some libraries) listed in LICENSING.md.

name: Grafana Loki

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004
GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 19 November 2007

editorial_view: Running Loki unmodified has no source obligation; modified versions offered to users over a network must offer their source under AGPL-3.0. Client libraries listed in LICENSING.md stay Apache-2.0.
notes: Named in the relicensing log's Grafana entry. Checked: v2.2.1 (Apache-2.0), v2.3.0 and v3.7.10 (AGPL). README: 'Grafana Loki is distributed under AGPL-3.0-only'.

name: Grafana Tempo

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004
GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 19 November 2007

editorial_view: Running Tempo unmodified has no source obligation; modified versions offered to users over a network must offer their source under AGPL-3.0.
notes: Named in the relicensing log's Grafana entry. Checked: v0.6.0 (Apache-2.0), v0.7.0, v1.0.0, v3.1.1 (AGPL). README: 'Grafana Tempo is distributed under AGPL-3.0-only'.

name: MinIO (community server)

eras.quote: Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004
GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 19 November 2007

editorial_view: The license is AGPL, but the bigger fact is that the community edition is no longer maintained: the repository is archived and the last community release is from October 2025. Plan a migration (for example to the Silo fork or another S3-compatible store) rather than new adoption.
notes:
The LICENSE file is the plain AGPL-3.0 text; the source file headers (checked cmd/server-main.go at RELEASE.2025-10-15T17-29-55Z) say 'either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version', hence AGPL-3.0-or-later. The BUSL Additional Use Grant covers only akka-streams as incorporated into Play Framework. The Change Date is updated per release (2.7.0 read 'TBD ( 3 years after 2.7.0 release )'). 'since' is the steward's dated public announcement where one exists, otherwise the date the LICENSE-changing commit landed.

eras.quote: Most is available under any one of the following: the Mozilla Public License (MPL), the GNU General Public License (GPL) and the GNU Lesser General Public License (LGPL).
most of the source code is available under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPL).

editorial_view: Firefox is MPL-2.0: file-level copyleft, so changes to Mozilla's files must be shared when distributed, while your own separate files can stay under your terms. The Firefox name and logo are trademarks not licensed by the MPL.
notes:
The root LICENSE only points to the about:license page (toolkit/content/license.html, now generated from license.html.mako) and disclaims trademark rights. Firefox 12.0's page states the MPL/GPL/LGPL tri-license (MPL 1.1); 13.0's states MPL 2.0, changed by commit bb8c314 (Bug 730814 'Update about:license to MPL 2', target milestone Firefox 13, milestone 13.0a1). Per-file headers moved in bulk later (commit cb6a072, Bug 716478 'MPL 2 upgrade: mozilla-central', 2012-05-21, which reached Firefox 15), so some files in 13 and 14 still carried tri-license headers. Era 1 was read from Mozilla's Mercurial host (hg-edge) because GitHub tags start at Firefox 46; its from=null covers Firefox 1.0 onward. The announcement is the Mozilla tracking bug (Bugzilla's web page blocked scripted access; the REST API confirmed it was resolved 2012-05-21). 'since' is the about:license commit date.
Steward detail: Mozilla Foundation (via Mozilla Corporation).

editorial_view: n8n has never been under an OSI-approved license. Since 0.169 the Sustainable Use License allows internal business, personal and non-commercial use but not offering n8n to others commercially, and files marked .ee need a paid n8n Enterprise License.
notes: Era 1 runs from the first public commit (2019-06-23, LICENSE already 'Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause', Licensor n8n GmbH from 2020) to 0.168.x; 0.169.0 is the first tag carrying the Sustainable Use License. The n8n Enterprise License for '.ee.' files was added on 2022-08-29 (LICENSE_EE.md) and is not modelled as a separate era because it does not change the license of the other code. The LICENSE also says content of branches other than master is not licensed. editorial_view: CockroachDB up to 19.1 is Apache-2.0 (core only), 19.2 to 24.2 are BUSL-1.1, and current releases use the proprietary CockroachDB Software License, which requires a license key and telemetry for production use. Late patch releases of 23.1 to 24.2 also moved to the new license, so check the LICENSE in the exact patch you run.
notes: Version boundaries are by release line, but patch releases cut after the 2024 change also carry the CockroachDB Software License: first such patches are v23.1.29, v23.2.16, v24.1.7 and v24.2.5 (each previous patch still says BSL). Since 2017 (v1.0, v1.1) the default build also included enterprise code under the CockroachDB Community License (CCL) in pkg/ccl; era 1 and era 2 expressions describe the default per-file license the LICENSE names, and CCL code is not modelled. At v1.0 the top-level LICENSE held the CCL agreement, which states the Community Edition is Apache-2.0. The 2019 announcement URL now returns 404 on cockroachlabs.com; it was verified through the Wayback Machine snapshot cited. The 2024 commit landed 2024-10-01; v24.3.0 was the first release under it. editorial_view: Couchbase Server source from 7.0 is BUSL-1.1 with a grant that allows production use but bars commercial derivative or hosted offerings; 6.6 and earlier source is Apache-2.0. Prebuilt Community and Enterprise binaries come with their own license agreements.
notes: Couchbase Server is assembled from many repositories (couchbase/manifest lists them); kv_engine, the data service, is used as the representative source and other repositories may differ. Era 1 is Not re-verified: before 7.0, kv_engine had no repository-level Apache LICENSE (its LICENSE was memcached's inherited Danga Interactive BSD notice), so Apache-2.0 rests on per-file headers such as the one cited. The change commit (2021-04-08) replaced that LICENSE with a statement naming BSL 1.1; licenses/BSL-Couchbase.txt followed on 2021-04-13 and is updated per release line (7.0, 7.1, 8.0). The announcement (Couchbase blog, 2021-03-26) returned 403 to scripted access and was verified through the Wayback snapshot cited. name: curl

eras.quote: Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software for any purpose with or without fee is hereby granted, provided that the above copyright notice

notes: Era starts at 7.10 (2002-10-01). curl's own docs/HISTORY.md (at curl-8_23_0) records earlier changes: GPL until 4.9 (1998), then MPL, then 'MIT (or MPL)' from 7.5.2 (January 2001), and 'October 1: with the release of curl 7.10 it is released under the MIT license only'.
